outcome: Give head of payments / chief risk officer a governed method to improve median alert investigation minutes using transaction ledgers, KYC profiles and sanction screening hits, with final decisions…
overview: AML Alert Investigation Workbench addresses operational records arrive through different systems, supervisors reconstruct evidence manually, and decisions are difficult to audit in banking and payments operations. The first proof of value uses transaction ledgers, KYC profiles and sanction screening hits. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is median alert investigation minutes, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: transaction ledgers, KYC profiles and sanction screening hits; define median alert investigation minutes and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Head of Payments / Chief Risk Officer.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including line-by-line reconciliations against known business transactions.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
